text:
yara: first week here, trying to finish k8s setup. downloaded kubeconfig from portal and merged into ~/.kube/config. now when i `kubectl config get-contexts` there are two named the same and i'm nervous about hitting prod. any quick way to tell which one points to prod vs dev?

mike: welcome! `kubectl config view -o jsonpath='{.contexts[*].name} {.contexts[*].context.cluster}'` shows the cluster arns. if the cluster name contains `prod` you'll see it. also `kubectl config get-contexts -o name` then `kubectl config view --raw -o jsonpath='{.clusters[?(@.name=="<cluster-name>")].cluster.server}'` to inspect the api-server url.

yara: ran that and one context's server is `api.k8s.redwood.prod.internal` so that was the dangerous one. i had `kubectl use-context redwood-dev` but it switched to the prod endpoint because of the name collision.

devex-bot: Heads up: docs/internal/onboarding/k8s#safe-merging has the recommended workflow: keep per-cluster files under `~/.kube/contexts/` and avoid merging. Use `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/contexts/dev.yaml:$KUBECONFIG` while working.

sre-mentor: i can help rename the context in your copied file so there's no collision. paste the output of `kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.users[0].name}'` (only the name needed).

yara: output is `yara@redwood`.

sre-mentor: done: created RoleBinding `onboard-yara-view` in namespace `team-data` binding `view` to `yara@redwood` for 3 days. please test `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n team-data` and then `kubectl get pods -n team-data`.

yara: `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n team-data` -> yes. `kubectl get pods -n team-data` shows pods. thanks! :tada:

mike: pro tip to avoid future collisions: before merging run `yq` to rewrite context and user names, e.g. `yq eval '.contexts[] |= ( .name = (.name + "-portal") )' portal.yaml` then add to contexts dir. also consider `kubectx` which shows human friendly names.

security-bot: Reminder: any traffic to prod will be audited. if you suspect accidental calls to prod, notify #incidents immediately.

yara: all good, no prod calls. i'll keep my kubeconfigs separated and update my shellrc with an alias to force dev-only: `alias kdev='KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/contexts/dev.yaml kubectl --context=redwood-dev-portal'`. thanks everyone, closing this thread.
